title: competition_standings double-counts Brasileirao seasons present in both league CSVs
evidence: src/service.ts:9 filters matches with normalize(m.competition).includes(normalize(competition)). Brasileirao_Matches.csv loads as competition 'Brasileirao' (src/data.ts:40) and novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv as 'Brasileirao historical' (src/data.ts:44); normalize('Brasileirao historical')='brasileirao historical' INCLUDES 'brasileirao', so standings('Brasileirao',2019) scans BOTH sources. Both files contain 380 matches for season 2019 (and all of 2012-2018 overlap), so every team's played/points/goals are doubled (~180 pts for the champion vs the real ~90). The standings mechanism IS implemented and computed from matches (not hardcoded), so this is partial, not missing. _factual.json scores 0.0 ('no tool returned a 2019 Serie A table naming Flamengo'). test/service.test.ts:14 only asserts table.length>10 and descending points, never a point total, so the defect passes CI.
suggestion: Give each match an explicit competition key and dedupe/choose one Brasileirao source per season, or require an exact competition match in standings() instead of substring includes().

title: Overlapping Brasileirao CSVs also inflate unfiltered team/aggregate/head-to-head stats
evidence: src/data.ts:39-45 loads both Brasileirao_Matches.csv and novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv with no dedup. teamStats (src/service.ts:7), aggregate (src/service.ts:11) and headToHead (src/service.ts:8) all run over this.data.matches, so for seasons 2012-2019 the duplicated Brasileirao fixtures are counted twice in R6/R10/R11 whenever no single-competition filter excludes one source.
suggestion: Deduplicate the two Brasileirao datasets at load time (prefer one as canonical per season).

title: Entire service/data logic compressed onto single lines
evidence: src/service.ts:6-11 each put a whole method on one line; idiomatic score 0.2 and maintainability 0.7432 in scores.json. Hurts readability/reviewability though it builds and tests pass.
suggestion: Format with the project formatter; split multi-statement one-liners.
